items.title: Johnny Lala Interview, 1960-03-15
items.q: I started off Tony Perranti. Tony Perranti. All of them big shots, man. ... I used to get to the carnival parade

ctx.x: Me is playing fine drum on you. He plays bass now, though. He's got a good impression. They won't let him play trombone because he's an old man. I know, but he plays bass now. He plays trombone better than anything. He got a good ear. Oh, yeah, man. We had some fun. I had some fun. I'll tell you, when you get him when he's right. I started off, listen. He plays a terrific trombone.

I started off Tony Perranti. Tony Perranti. All of them big shots, man. I can't have all of them. You know what I used to do is I used to get to the carnival parade, you know? I'm getting close. Who's the guy knocked on Santos' door when he first got a trombone? Yeah, it wasn't you, huh?
Faith. Faith? Yeah. Who's that? He's not talking about Faith Mara, boy. No, he ain't a good story on the television. Oh, I don't know. They winsteyn's program, hey?
